Subject: Renewal discussion — Novalign term coming up in Jan

Hi Clara / Tom,

Hope you're both well. Novalign's current commitment term ends 01-Feb-2027. I wanted to start the renewal conversation early so we can line up procurement timelines on your side and avoid any service interruption.

High level we see two levers that typically work for customers of your scale: a phased capacity uplift (so you can ramp without a big upfront commit) paired with a limited price hold/credit in the first 6 months to give you breathing room as usage normalizes.

Would you be open to a 24-month renewal with a year-1 committed baseline + a scheduled uplift on month 7 (automatic) and a one-time underutilization credit if year-1 usage is below 85% of the baseline? If that sounds sensible I can draft a short term sheet and get Finance involved for approval.

If you'd prefer to keep the same structure but ask for a year-2 step increase instead, let me know which you prefer (phased bump vs. stepped commit). Happy to jump on a 30-min call next week.

Best,

- Q4 was lighter than expected due to a delayed pilot; we expect Q1-2027 to ramp.

Monica / Markus — forwarding Clara's reply and the context. Key asks: concrete year-1 price hold, size of one-time credit, and a cap on exposure. They are open to a phased uplift but procurement timeline is tight (30 days).

My preliminary thoughts:
- Offer a 12-month price hold at current unit rate for year-1, then a scheduled uplift of +25% committed GPU-hours on month 7 (year-1) to transition them gradually to target commit.
- One-time credit equal to 7% of year-1 committed value if utilization < 85%.
- Add an SLA clause for latency parity during uplift; if we miss 99th p90 targets twice in a rolling 30-day window provide correction credits.

Can Finance/Legal bless the 7% credit and the +25% phased bump? If not, what are the ceilings we can offer without exec sign-off?

Thanks,
Avery

Quick answer: we can approve the structure with the following guardrails. Finance reviewed and provided concessions that are within our standard renewal playbook.

Proposed concession package (approved up to VP):
- Term: 24 months.
- Year-1: hold current unit pricing (no increase) through month 6.
- Month 7: automatic uplift of +20% committed capacity (not 25%) — this reduces our exposure while still giving Novalign runway.
- One-time utilization credit: 6% of year-1 committed spend if utilization < 85%. Credit applies as account-level refund or future-credit at customer's election.
- Exposure cap: Redwood's maximum liability limited to the credit above + one month of service fees.
- SLA: include latency parity clause; operational correction credits capped at 2% of monthly invoice per event, not to exceed 6%/quarter.

We should attach a short term sheet reflecting these numbers and offer a DocuSign route for quick signature. If customer pushes for a larger credit or higher price hold beyond month 6 we escalate to Sales Ops.

Markus
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
